records.reason: m40 at 10/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 8.31/19.38 mL. Pairing it with the selected 20/1 condition tests the steep predicted transition for this naphthyl ketone and fills the gap before its measured late 50/1 regime.

m40 at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 22.51/38.42 mL and has high current CW distance. Together with the selected 10/1 point, it distinguishes gradual retention growth from a localized transition and tests transfer from simpler aromatic ketones.

m29 at 50/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 9.80/24.22 mL. Its measured 10/1 condition remains relatively early. This extension tests whether the crowded acetyl environment limits onset growth compared with less hindered aromatic ketones.

m33 at 50/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 12.89/29.99 mL. Existing lower-ratio measurements establish a useful response series. This endpoint extends that curve and provides a methyl-substitution comparison with selected m29 and measured acetophenone conditions.

m68 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 6.29/13.85 mL. Its measured finishes at 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1 are nonmonotonic. A stronger-eluent point helps determine whether the broad 5/1 finish is localized and constrains transfer from other extended aromatic ketones.

m53 at 0/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 9.23/19.20 mL, later than its measured 2/1 behavior. Measuring this pure-EA endpoint directly tests a questionable strong-eluent baseline for an unsaturated aldehyde.

m53 at 1/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 10.86/22.71 mL, also later than its measured 2/1 behavior. The matched selected 0/1 point distinguishes a persistent strong-eluent regime from a narrow prediction reversal without imposing monotonicity as an absolute rule.

m53 at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 19.91/45.80 mL. It fills the large gap between measured 5/1 and late 50/1 conditions, complementing the strong-eluent tests with supervision for the upper part of the same scaffold's response.

m28 at 1/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 7.18/22.19 mL. Existing 2/1, 5/1, and 10/1 measurements show substantial finish growth. This missing anchor tests whether broad V2 behavior begins before the major onset delay.

m94 at 2/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 9.65/18.55 mL. It extends a fixed-loading series containing measured 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1 conditions and tests how this cyclopropyl beta-ketoester enters its late-retention regime.

m95 at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 17.84/51.90 mL. Comparison with its measured 150-uL condition and ethyl acetoacetate at the same ratio and sample volume tests whether ester substitution and loading affect onset and finish differently.

m107 at 0/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 5.55/10.27 mL. Its measured 1/1, 2/1, and 5/1 conditions are substantially later. This pure-EA anchor tests whether its broad-tail regime is strongly condition-dependent rather than an intrinsically late baseline.

m86 at 2/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 14.31/26.98 mL. Pairing it with the selected 5/1 condition holds all loading fields fixed and tests the para-amino ester's response before its predicted sharp delay.

m86 at 5/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 38.10/74.58 mL. This uncovered high-sensitivity condition, paired with 2/1, tests whether the para-amino ester develops a sharp transition comparable to the measured meta ester. Cross-isomer interpretation must retain their different loading conditions.

m89 at 20/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 22.87/43.66 mL. Its recent 100-uL counterpart was overpredicted at acquisition. This added loading level tests whether the response is amount-dependent and limits inappropriate upward corrections across amino esters.

m104 at 5/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 5.97/14.81 mL. It supplies a lower-ratio reference at the same loading as the recent 20/1 measurement with a large V2 underestimate, testing whether the long finish emerges only at weaker eluent.

m104 at 20/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 8.82/18.68 mL. Its measured 50- and 100-uL finishes differ substantially. This third loading level tests an endpoint-specific amount relationship rather than assuming the latest low-loading tail applies everywhere.

m87 at 2/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 7.87/15.95 mL. Its measured 100- and 150-uL records have substantially different V2 values. The missing lower-loading label helps distinguish a systematic amount response from isolated record variability in a methoxybenzoate.

m75 at 20/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 12.72/23.03 mL. Its measured 100-uL condition was later, while the recent 10/1 result was well predicted. This label tests whether the delayed intermediate-ratio regime persists at another loading level.

m67 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 9.65/13.74 mL. The measured 150-uL condition was much earlier, while its 100-uL 10/1 and 20/1 conditions were later. This point locates the onset delay and tests whether the early result reflects loading or local variability.

m67 at 5/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 13.34/19.68 mL. It bridges measured 2/1 and 20/1 conditions at the same loading. Recent opposite-sign endpoint errors motivate separate calibration of onset growth and finish growth.

m60 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 14.03/19.32 mL. Its measured 5/1 and 10/1 conditions are substantially later. This lower-ratio point tests a nonbenzylic secondary alcohol; comparison with selected benzylic m67 must account for their different loading solvents.

m51 at 2/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 13.17/20.06 mL. Existing 5/1 and 10/1 measurements establish delayed behavior. This condition tests whether a tertiary nonbenzylic alcohol follows the mild early m203 response or develops retention at stronger eluent.

m119 at 0/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 7.16/13.13 mL. Its same-loading 2/1 measurement is substantially later. This strong-eluent endpoint tests whether the ether-containing alcohol already has a raised baseline in pure EA.

m119 at 1/1 and 150 uL is predicted at approximately 11.16/22.47 mL. Together with the selected pure-EA condition and existing 2/1 and 5/1 measurements, it constrains the strong-eluent side of this alcohol family's response while retaining loading differences in interpretation.

m209 at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 18.56/47.92 mL. Its measured 100-uL condition and the loading-dependent onset shifts of iodophenol provide references. This tests whether the endpoint pattern transfers to a different phenolic environment.

m216 at 1/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 11.03/25.82 mL. Measured 5/1 and 10/1 conditions at this loading are much later. The new point locates the response threshold of a basic fused heteroaromatic without transferring the phenylpyridine curve wholesale.

m45 at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 13.50/26.56 mL. It fills the same-loading gap between measured 2/1 and 10/1 conditions and tests the acid's earlier solvent response independently of its anomalous 50/1 record.

m173 at 0/1 with 2000 uL loading solvent is predicted at approximately 7.37/27.38 mL. A nearly matched measured record uses 1500 uL loading solvent. Existing 2000-uL records at other ratios make this useful for testing loading-solvent-volume effects beyond sample amount.

m191 at 1/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 5.53/21.63 mL. Its measured 5/1 and 10/1 conditions show strong retention growth. This missing strong-eluent label tests whether a dialdehyde retains an early onset while already exhibiting a long finish.

m73 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at approximately 5.42/11.57 mL. Its ordinary measured 0/1 result and weaker-eluent records motivate this intermediate anchor. The label can constrain interpolation without interpreting other reversed-endpoint records as a chemical mechanism.

m156 at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at approximately 6.57/16.20 mL. Existing 1/1 and 50/1 measurements bracket early retention and a longer finish. This fills the intervening regime for a donor-free, acceptor-free fluorinated aromatic and tests V2 growth without substantial onset delay.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response curvature and the relationship between onset and finish are scaffold-specific. A shared solvent correction cannot reliably transfer among aromatic ketones, carbonyl-rich esters, aldehydes, acids, and basic heteroaromatics.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Linked labels can teach where retention growth begins and whether it affects V1, V2, or both, limiting inappropriate transfer of broad-tail corrections into ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m40 10/1–20/1 pair and the added lower-ratio carbonyl references reveal smooth local curves or sharp scaffold-specific transitions?

hypotheses.content: Loading-associated endpoint changes may depend on molecule and eluent regime. The predictor's near invariance across many candidate sample-volume contrasts warrants testing, while ordinary measured contrasts and repeated-condition variability caution against a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts can distinguish learnable changes in onset or finish from variability that additional structural complexity cannot explain. Sample amount remains the supplied density-times-sample-volume feature; loading-solvent volume is a separate recorded condition.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the new m104, m89, m87, m75, and m209 loading levels show coherent endpoint shifts, and does m173 show a loading-solvent-volume effect under pure EA?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl presence alone does not determine the solvent-response curve. Benzylic versus nonbenzylic placement, substitution around the alcohol, additional ether groups, and recorded loading conditions require local calibration.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The recent ordinary m203 results and later alcohol families argue for conditional transfer instead of a common hydrogen-bond-donor delay. Missing lower-ratio labels can identify where those families diverge.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At the added 0/1–5/1 conditions, do m67, m60, m51, and m119 enter delayed retention at different solvent strengths?

hypotheses.content: Amino-benzoate response depends on positional environment and loading conditions. The sharp meta-ester delay around 5/1 should not automatically be transferred to ortho esters; the para ester's corresponding transition remains insufficiently measured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Opposite acquisition-error directions for m89 and m104 make a family-wide upward tail correction unreliable. The fixed-loading m86 ratio pair provides a cleaner local response experiment than cross-isomer comparisons with different loading solvents.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m86 show the predicted large 2/1-to-5/1 transition, and is m104's long low-loading finish already present at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: The current m53 predictions at pure EA and 1/1 may reflect a mislearned strong-eluent baseline: both are later than its measured 2/1 behavior. Chemical expectations favor earlier elution with stronger PE/EA mobile phase, but the actual local relationship remains unmeasured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two matched strong-eluent labels can distinguish a real catalog relationship from a prediction reversal and improve interpolation for unsaturated aldehydes without imposing a hard monotonic rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 100-uL loading, are m53's 0/1 and 1/1 endpoints earlier than, similar to, or later than its measured 2/1 endpoints?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback supports endpoint-specific repair. m104 at 20/1 and 50 uL had a nearly correct onset but a 12.33-mL acquisition-time V2 underestimate, whereas m89 at 20/1 and 100 uL had a 9.36-mL V2 overestimate. This weakens a shared amino-ester tail correction. The m203 pure-EA and 5/1 results were relatively close to their predictions, and its 2/1 finish was overpredicted, weakening a blanket late-retention assumption for alcohols. m67 at 20/1 and 150 uL combined an onset overestimate with a finish underestimate, motivating separate endpoint calibration. The latest m42 weak-eluent result remained later than predicted, while m4 retained an early onset and broader finish. Ordinary references, including m109 at 20/1, mostly showed smaller errors, reducing the value of indiscriminate additional baseline or loading measurements. These historical errors guide questions but are not current-model residuals. Earlier condition descriptions also require correction: 0/1 denotes pure EA; the loading-solvent field does not specify the mobile phase; sample volume and loading-solvent volume are distinct.
batch_rationale: The unchanged 32-experiment batch concentrates on uncovered relationships within represented molecules. The m40 pair and m53 series test solvent-response shape; substituted ketones and carbonyl-rich ester anchors test transfer across structural environments. Amino-ester experiments address a recent endpoint-specific failure while testing its dependence on ratio and loading. Alcohol labels locate earlier response thresholds rather than repeating characterized late conditions. Selected loading contrasts connect informative measured endpoints, and m173 probes loading-solvent volume separately from sample amount. The m73 point constrains an ambiguous local region without interpreting reversed endpoint records as a mechanism. A fluorinated aromatic reference tests finish growth in a low-polarity family. These linked experiments may improve Row-distribution accuracy by teaching conditional interactions and limiting overextension of exceptional tails. Quantile widths and CW distance are supporting model signals, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; elution interval width is not prediction uncertainty.
